notes.title: Update 004: Track Switching
notes.notes: [p][b]Update 004 Topics[/b][/p][list][*][p]Track Switching (long winded)[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Auto Testing[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][b]Track Switching 🔀[/b][/p][p]One cool aspect of developing Railborn is the unique design challenges we come across. One of these seemed trivial at first, but became more complicated as we started to conjure up the answer: how does the player switch tracks?[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/b1b3a5a700d230ace9e4ad09d1ada7ae01bcdfe6.jpg"][/img][/p][p]A couple of challenges:[/p][list][*][p]Life would be simpler if [b]Railborn’s[/b] train had a “front” – like Zelda Spirit Tracks. But – since we allow piece by piece building of your train, you decide what is the “front”, not us! Therefore, when we present the player “left” or “right” what is this all relative to?[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]UI! How do we present the player the UI to switch tracks? Again, most games would probably pop up an interactive menu – but again, we want players to have the ability to build their train's controlling [b]components[/b] piece by piece in the location they choose. Making your own cockpit is cool.[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]So how do we do this? [b]Track Switcher[/b][/p][p]The [b]Track Switcher[/b] is a built item that has a digital display. The player can switch it to go left, straight or right. The display will always show the [b]upcoming [/b]intersection path options.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/c5f90cddfa5b6402d78abd1b7946fb296e69429e.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]How do we tell you what is the next intersection? Alright – we’re trying out an in-world icon that displays the distance and path choices so you have an idea of what’s coming up. In the example below you can see next intersection is in 48 meters, and one can go left or straight. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/018d067f19bb75eb21f41dc7139b6767446a5b6c.gif"][/img][/p][p] [/p][p]Switching in action [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/d2a0263c90d47ebedfa636e809bfdafad0784033.gif"][/img][/p][p] [/p][p]Let’s get weird. So here, you can see the train changing what it considers “front” depending on the direction of travel.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/0b73fb9eaa0ec038d98ce518cf2103a5beb82a68.gif"][/img][/p][p] [/p][p]So, what happens when your [b]Track Switcher[/b] is facing the opposite direction of what your train thinks is front (again remember, front changes with direction of travel). Well – the display on the [b]Track Switcher[/b] will always display the upcoming intersection in the direction of travel.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/23da808172ced4223258baea7cc8179b17a1f2c9.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Let’s see this in action:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/d4c1ef77c61b0e0bc287b5b92f5f7b4b62bbb486.gif"][/img][/p][p] [/p][p]If that seems a bit too tricky for you – we have an easy solution (which I use) – it is to build another Track Switcher facing the other direction! All your track switchers synchronize direction, so now deciding which way to go is much simpler. Check it out:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/b9bce6213075b23ad3c3ff1c3dc605058367aa99.gif"][/img][/p][p] [/p][p]This is what we have in mind, although once your, the Early Access brave souls get your hands on Railborn, might change.[/p][p] [/p][p] [/p][p][b]Auto Testing 🧪[/b][/p][p]Well, this wouldn’t be an update post if there wasn’t a boring technical part. We have set up a slick little system that builds the Railborn after every check-in to our repository. We then automatically load up Railborn on our trusty old laptop equipped with a 1660 Ti - our minimum spec target. [/p][p][/p][p]The test performs a few in-game operations then spits back the performance with respect to FPS, Draw calls, GPU usage, along with a few other nifty benchmarks (below). This is really handy because it lets us know which new addition to the game caused a performance hitch. It easily can be that performance suffers from a feature or addition you had no idea would be a problem. Anyway, here is a chart of our last 20 check-ins. 😊[/p][p]Note cells that turn red are over our threshold for our minimum spec target and that build should be investigated.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/27a625e2a7857a1e5acd0315531df7ff5081d7be.png"][/img][/p][p] [/p][p]As always, please shoot out our [b]game link to some friends for a Wishlist or two[/b] 😊 [/p][p][/p][p]Smashlore & Taky[/p]

notes.title: Ambient Occlusion - Huh?
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/bdc8f9d39107e44472ae343e3c217e3566d093a7.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Welcome back! It is that time I like to share a few interesting topics about what we’ve been diligently working on. I’ll admit, this post is more technical than some people probably want. I promise to have more gameplay topics soon enough![/p][p][/p][p][b]Update 003 Topics[/b][/p][list][*][p]Custom Material[/p][/*][*][p]Streaming Tech[/p][/*][*][p]Target GPU[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][b]Custom Material 🌲[/b][/p][p]Optimization and performance are really important for us. We love the Unreal Engine – but it is too easy to develop games for the highest end computers. Therefor in order to provide players the experience they deserve we have lots of tricks up our sleeve. For example, we made a custom material for [i]Ambient Occlusion[/i] when rendering our MANY foliage in the game. The who what?[/p][p][/p][p]Here is a screenshot of some sample woods that contains our low poly foliage – great performance, but lack luster looks. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/ec3dcf53cb162a8aa8d39f79a8738039f155e902.png"][/img][/p][p]Our custom material pre-generates an [i]Ambient Occlusion[/i] layer for these trees with a snowy looking algorithm that takes into account how far the branch is from the trunk, and the type of leaves on the tree. You can see the gradient change the farther a branch is from the tree, and also the difference the leaves on the Aspen generate (bottom left).[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/9dd86ebbd19ceffb882aaa7bd0f70c77cceaa291.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Adding this is we now can achieve the look we want with the performance we need.[/p][p] [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/4cbe020863110befa53f742e5f39f8eccd8d215f.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/c7ef8b091239dc76d53e4291ee2b73c21885db1b.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Streaming Tech 🚿[/b][/p][p]Railborn has some unique development challenges compared to other games. One of these is how quickly you can eventually travel through the world on your train. We therefor are required to load the world much quicker than if the player was simply moving on foot. (that’s right – most games only load in the part of the world the player is standing in). So how do we handle loading 1000’s of objects into the world without hitching?[/p][p][/p][p]Well – we created a [i]SuperItemSystem[/i] that hydrates! All our objects are placed into giant chunks – so we don’t load a gazillion static meshes but instead dehydrated data nodes! (see pic - yellow outlined trees is a single chunk)[/p][p] [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/9338c4b78aefe544854315fb6e9480689b08848b.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Every time a player travels near on foot or train we can now load 30000 objects in as a single node. As the player gets close enough to interact, we hydrate these data nodes with digital water so they can now be interacted with and be part of the world! The idea here is to prevent hitching as you explore Railborn.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]Target GPU 🖥️[/b][/p][p]Every game should have a performance target! Our target for Railborn is a 1660 Ti for Medium settings at 60fps. Yes, we do have an army of 1660 Ti laptops that run the game every morning. 😊 We chose this target after consulting with the Steam hardware survey as a balance between accessibility for players and resources for us to make an awesome game. Of course, the resolution you’re playing at and other factors can make it easier to play on less powerful machines.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/145de26f13117c8b15bb12c743eb700baaedae24.jpg"][/img][/p][p] [/p][p]Fewf. A lot of technical stuff. If you made it this far – cool! And as a reminder, please shoot out our game link to some friends for a [b]Wishlist[/b] or two 😊 Or even better, chat about us.[/p][p][/p][p]Smashlore & Taky[/p]

notes.title: Update #002: Rooftop Runs
notes.notes: [p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/5a814ea68f961f9f999f6ea29da1590b9846758b.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Well – I’m going to come right out and say it – the last month has been fantastic for the future of Railborn. Since we announced just a little while ago we have had a huge amount of interest from players like you – which means others share our vision! This is 1) motivating 2) exciting 3) tells us people want the type of game we want. Reception outside of Steam has also been [url="https://www.tiktok.com/@madmorph/video/7518443211350723862"]mega positive[/url]! [/p][p] [/p][p]If you are new with Washbear – every official update I choose a select [b]few[/b] topics to discuss. We have been working on so much – but for the sake of all our time, I pick just a couple of thoughts.[/p][p] [/p][h3]Update 002 Topics[/h3][list][*][p]Wishlists[/p][/*][*][p]VRAM[/p][/*][*][p]Rooftop Running[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h3]Wishlists🎊[/h3][p]How is this even a topic? Well it is! I’d provide you with an actual Wishlist update but the Steam backend seems to be having a hiccup, so I’ll save that for later this week. Needless to say you all have been AMAZING. I can’t stress enough how Wishlists contribute to the success of Railborn. So if you have a moment, [b]please pass on the Railborn store page[/b] to your friend groups for a Wishlist. Alright, enough begging for Wishlists. 😊[/p][p] [/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2340970/Railborn/"][/dynamiclink][/p][h3]VRAM 🐏[/h3][p]As a Steam user, I mostly enjoy updates that feature cool graphics or new mechanics. Truthfully though from the dev side – we often have a lot of “difficult to show off” work to do that is REALLY important. Our target for Railborn is to run smoothly at a High graphic setting with 4 GB video RAM. We decided on this target by looking at the Steam survey[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/4ca1e2ec47b982ecf73dce6ee1359655eeb715b3.png"][/img][/p][p]This means going deep into how we texture the world of Railborn to find efficiencies. Is there a lot of whiteboard madness tracking where every precious VRAM GB goes? Yes – there is. We come from a console background of game development so we like to statically allocate all of our textures and stream in only what we have to. This makes the game much smoother and minimize hitches.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/c795319b7f4922304b3a58b93ae270ebae5bb4c6.jpg"][/img][/p][p] [/p][h3]Roof Running 👟[/h3][p]In Railborn you can expand your home by unlocking and building additional train cars. Each train car can have a different style (dictated by you) and purpose (again, decided by you). Moving between train cars can be done via doors – or – my favorite – running across the roofs. When we had started making Railborn I knew this was a feature we had to have! To be clear, this was difficult from a technical point of view (I’ll save this for another post). Here is an extended version of running rooftops.[/p][p] [/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45652029/46adbf7593169b4b92b3ca6252d577b777f3f66e.gif"][/img] [/p][p]The key is ensuring you build parts of your train cart roofs that are flat, and have a little point to enable you land on the next train car. I can’t wait to see all the ideas you folks come up with![/p][p] [/p][p] [/p][p]That’s it for now. Be safe our there friends! (and remember to grab us some Wishlists 😊)[/p][p][/p][p]xoxo Smashlore & Taky[/p][p] [/p]

notes.title: Update #001:🚆🦖Railborn
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/6c1f2baa52448890ec9a2c3006a165317fc9aba1.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Hi all! Welcome to our first Update for [i]Railborn[/i]! 🎉🎉 If you’re new to the Washbear family – our first game was [url=""]Parkasaurus[/url]. [b]🦖[/b][/p][p] [/p][p]Railborn has been in development for 2 years now – and we are very excited (relieved?) to finally be able to share what we’ve been working on. Just like with [i]Parkasaurus[/i], we plan to develop [i]Railborn[/i] alongside our community, taking feedback and ideas.💡 I know, I know, a lot of developers say that - but we [i]actually[/i] mean it. We've [i]proved[/i] this with our development of [i]Parkasaurus. [/i]Ask any of our community. [/p][p][/p][p]Our community was the rock solid foundation 🪨 that helped make [i]Parkasaurus[/i] a success, and with your help we hope to do it again with [i]Railborn[/i]🤘[i]. [/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/72dd631b7ddb4eb3b85540b91e9655728506b5df.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The first HUGE favor you can do for us (yes, you will hear me drone on about this a LOT 🙄) is to:[/p][p][/p][h3][url=""]Wishlist Railborn and pass on the link to your friends![/url][/h3][p][/p][p]Why? Well – Wishlists are really important to let Steam know people are interested in the game, and also let us make the game bigger and better. So – more Wishlists, better awesomer game. (awesomer IS a word I swear).[/p][p] [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/af9994d10f0d96ded73fb3877a4ea463e1ddfe6d.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Please feel free to hang out with us in our Discord or follow us on our manyyy socials.[/p][p][/p][p]I like to update regularly with what’s new in development here – so expect a lot of random thoughts and screenshots of what we’re doing.[/p][p] [/p][p]I’m happy you’re here with us and look forward to this adventure![/p][p] [/p][p]xoxo Smashlore & Taky[/p]
